name: Georgia

code.name: Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)
code.edition: not read: the Code itself could not be reached; the rules below rest on Acts of the General Assembly published on state sites and on a state agency guide, each flagged on its section

ga-sb3ex.citation: Georgia S.B. 3EX (2026 special session), Section 2, adding subsection (d.1) to Code Section 21-2-495 (recount procedure); text of the Act as passed
ga-sb3ex.note: An Act's text, read as a PDF download on the Governor's site under 'signed legislation'; it is not the Code as the Code's publisher prints it. Each line of the PDF carries a line number, so quotations cut at line ends with [...].

ga-sb202.citation: Georgia House Substitute to Senate Bill 202 (2021), Section 42, revising Code Section 21-2-501 (number of votes required for election; runoff)
ga-sb202.note: A BILL's text (the House substitute), not the Code in force and not the Act as finally enacted. The bill prints deleted and inserted words together (for example '(7)(2)' and 'were are'), so only sentences untouched by that marking are quoted. It is the nearest text of 21-2-501 on a state site; it was read to find what the section says, and may have been amended since. Each line carries a line number, so quotations cut at line ends with [...].

ga-guide-recount.citation: Georgia.gov, 'Election Recount Rules in Georgia' (state agency guide, not the statute)
ga-guide-recount.note: A guide on the State's portal; lower grade than the statute. It cites Georgia H.B. 316 (2019), which was not itself read.

ties.applies_to: any primary, special primary, election or special election for public office in which no candidate receives a majority
ties.steps: no candidate is nominated or elected without a majority of the votes cast; where no candidate receives a majority, a run-off between the candidates with the two highest numbers of votes is held; the highest vote in the runoff wins (the bill text sets the runoff dates: the ninth week after a primary or a federal general election, the twenty-eighth day after other general elections)
ties.who: not stated in the text read

sources.quote: In instances where no candidate receives a majority of the [...] votes cast, a run-off primary, special primary runoff, run-off election, or special election [...] runoff between the candidates receiving the two highest numbers of votes shall be held.

In the case of a runoff from a general election for a federal office [...] or special election for a federal office held in conjunction with a general [...] election, the runoff shall be held on the Tuesday of the ninth week following such general [...] election.

In the case of a runoff from a general election for an office other than a federal office [...] or a runoff from a special primary or special election for an office other than a federal [...] office held in conjunction with a general election, the runoff shall be held on the [...] twenty-eighth day after the day of holding the preceding general or special primary or [...] general or special election.

ties.note: The text does not use the word 'tie' and does not say what happens when the two highest numbers are equal. A tied two-candidate contest leaves no candidate with a majority, so a runoff between the same two follows [inferred]; for more than two tied candidates, or a tie for second place, the text read gives no rule. Municipal charters may provide for election by plurality (subsection (b) of the same section), in which case this runoff does not apply to that municipality; charters were not read. The text is a bill, not the Code in force (see the section's note), so the rule is marked inferred and the Code should be read before any figure rests on it.
Not found in the text that could be read, and the Code itself could not be read, so no absence is claimed. See 'unread'.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes which were cast in such qualified contest
threshold.conditions: only a 'qualified contest': a general election contest for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, Attorney General, State School Superintendent, Commissioner of Insurance, Commissioner of Agriculture or Commissioner of Labor that appears as the first or second contest on the ballot; a manual recount of all ballots in all counties, directed by the Secretary of State no later than two business days after the certification date
threshold.in_words: a margin of not more than one-half of one percent of the votes cast in a statewide executive contest that is the first or second contest on the ballot makes a manual recount of all ballots mandatory

who_may_request: no request: the Secretary of State directs it
recounts.cost_bearer: the state, which reimburses counties' reasonable costs if the county superintendent completes the recount within seventeen days of the Secretary of State ordering it

sources.quote: in any qualified contest that appears as the first or second contest on a ballot, the [...] difference between the number of votes received by a candidate who has been declared [...] elected to an office in such qualified contest and the number of votes received by any [...] other candidate or candidates not declared so elected shall be not more than one-half of [...] 1 percent of the total votes which were cast in such qualified contest.

the term 'qualified contest' shall mean a [...] general election contest for the offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of [...] State, Attorney General, State School Superintendent, Commissioner of Insurance, [...] Commissioner of Agriculture, and Commissioner of Labor.
The state shall reimburse counties the reasonable costs incurred by such counties in [...] any recount conducted pursuant to this subsection

recounts.note: From an Act of the 2026 special session, read as a PDF on the Governor's 'signed legislation' page, adding subsection (d.1) to 21-2-495; the page's heading is the only sign here that the Act was signed. The Code as printed by its publisher was not read. 'Notwithstanding any provisions of subsection (c)', so it sits beside the requested recount below. Contests other than the eight offices (for example U.S. Senate and House, the legislature) are not covered by this rule.

threshold.percent_of: not stated in the guide (the margin)
threshold.conditions: the request must be made within two business days of the results being certified; the guide names no office limit
threshold.in_words: a candidate can request a recount if the margin is less than or equal to one-half of one percent, within two business days of certification

sources.quote: State law does not require an automatic recount of votes. However, based on Georgia H.B. 316 (2019), a candidate can request a recount if the margin is less than or equal to 0.5%. That request has to be made within two business days of the results being certified.

recounts.note: From a state agency guide (Georgia.gov), not from the statute; the guide's 'no automatic recount' sentence is overtaken for the eight statewide executive offices by the 2026 Act above. The guide says nothing of primaries, presidential electors or measures, which are not recorded as covered. The guide also says an election official, or the Secretary of State on a candidate's petition about a suspected error or discrepancy, can ask for a recount; those are not margin rules and are not recorded.

notes: Georgia is partly read. The tie rule rests on a bill's text (flagged), the requested recount on a state agency guide (lower grade, flagged), and the automatic recount on a 2026 Act. The Code's own text should be fetched before any of it is shown as law. The Secretary of State's rule 183-1-15-.03 (Georgia Rules and Regulations, rules.sos.ga.gov) was read: it sets recount procedure, not the margin that triggers one, and is not cited.

Earlier reader's lead (research/historical-close-races-v2.md 3a and 3b): 'runoff in 28 days' as the tie rule and 'automatic at 0.5% in the first or second statewide executive races' were UNREAD there. The automatic recount is now borne out by the 2026 special-session Act (S.B. 3EX); the 28 days applies to a non-federal general election runoff and a federal one is on the ninth week's Tuesday (S.B. 202 substitute text).
